newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower as soybeans falter.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower as soybeans falter.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended lower on Tuesday, keying off of losses in soybeans linked to outlooks for a cool week and wet weekend in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.

Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio said temperatures would be below normal on Tuesday with a gradual warm-up expected into the weekend. A storm system was forecast to bring 0.25 to 1.00 inch of rain with 40 to 60 percent coverage on Sunday or Monday, Burgio said.
Forecasts diverged after the weekend with some predicting another dry spell while others saw increased moisture.

Some meteorologists said a ridge of high pressure would move west, opening the door for more moisture to reach the central Corn Belt. That ridge had been keeping rainfall away from some areas of Missouri, Illinois and Indiana and crops in those regions are in need of moisture.
The National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook also suggested a wetter week ahead with below normal temperatures and above normal rainfall across much of the U.S. Midwest.
Soymeal ended $4.20 to $1.50 per ton lower with December down $3.10 at $210.20. Soyoil closed 0.28 to 0.15 cent per lb lower with December down 0.25 at 22.34.

On the day, Merrill Lynch bought 400 lots December soymeal and 100 August, Smith Barney bought 400 December and Tenco Inc and FIMAT Futures each bought 300 December, traders said. Merrill Lynch also sold 200 December, as did Tenco and R.J. O'Brien, traders said. Cargill Inc and ADM were also said to be sellers.
In soyoil, Prudential Securities sold 400 lots December and Produce Grain sold 500 December while ADM and Cargill were light buyers on the September, floor sources said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 21,000 lots, compared with Monday's actual volume of 21,203 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 19,000 lots, against Monday's 19,314.
